title: workflow policy: every GitHub Actions workflow must declare top-level concurrency, enforced by the rego deny rule deny_workflow_without_concurrency
answers: A workflow file fails the policy check with a message that it must declare 'concurrency' explicitly; what do I add?
How do I add concurrency to a new or existing GitHub Actions workflow in this repo?
Where is the workflow policy that requires concurrency enforced, and why would a new event not cancel older runs?
body:
Path: .github/policy.rego:deny_workflow_without_concurrency is the conftest-style deny rule that scans every workflow under .github/workflows; it fires when a file has `input.jobs` (so composite actions with `runs` are exempt) and no top-level `input.concurrency`.
Rule: Every workflow file must declare a top-level `concurrency:` block. The repo's placeholder for workflows with no meaningful grouping yet is `group: ${{ github.run_id }}` with `cancel-in-progress: false`, which makes each run its own group, so it never supersedes or waits on another run. Grouping by `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` is the standard choice when new events should supersede in-flight runs. The rule's message lists both options.
Symptom: Without a concurrency block a new event never supersedes runs already in flight, so stale runs keep consuming runners and repo-mutating workflows can race.
Constraints: Only checked on workflow files (`input.jobs` present); composite actions are not required to declare it. The run_id placeholder is an opt-out, not a grouping decision; replacing it with a real group is a follow-up per the PR. Placement convention used by the 29 workflows is directly after the `on:` block and before `defaults:`.
applies: Any workflow file under .github/workflows that the workflow policy check evaluates; not composite actions.
says: Older pipeline runs keep executing and wasting build runners after newer commits are pushed.
Simultaneous automated build jobs are racing and conflicting when modifying shared repository state.
The automated pull request check fails stating that workflow concurrency must be declared explicitly.
Automatically cancel in-flight test runs whenever a contributor pushes updates to their pull request.
Enforce a rule requiring all automation pipelines to specify how concurrent runs are handled.

Workflows can use the run_id placeholder group: ${{ github.run_id }} with cancel-in-progress: false, or group by ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }} to cancel in-flight runs.
